If this switch is on, GET requests without a valid sign-in or API key are no longer possible either – regardless of the publication status of individual records. Files of the media library remain reachable via their address. The switch is saved at once.

Every newly set password must have at least this many characters (creating a user, changing the password). Existing passwords stay valid; the hint text and the password generator follow the rule. Default: 8, allowed: {min} to {max}.
New passwords must contain at least one digit. Default: on.
New passwords must contain at least one character that is neither a letter nor a digit nor whitespace (e.g. ! ? # - _). Default: on.
New passwords must contain at least one upper-case and one lower-case letter. Default: off.

A sign-in stays valid for this long, counted from the login – regardless of activity. After that a new sign-in is required. Applies at once, to sessions already running as well. Default: 8, allowed: {min} to {max} (30 days).

This many wrong passwords are allowed per username and per IP address within the time window; the next attempt is rejected – even with the correct password. Also applies to the current password when changing the password. Default: 5, allowed: {min} to {max}.
Failed attempts count for this long, so a lock lasts at most this long as well. Default: 15, allowed: {min} to {max} (24 hours).
Older rows of the table login_attempts are deleted on every sign-in. Only the time window counts for the lock; a longer retention merely serves traceability. Default: 1, allowed: {min} to {max}.
The media library rejects larger files on upload; existing files are not affected. Default: 20 (or MEDIA_MAX_MB from config.php), allowed: {min} to {max}.
The server currently allows at most {size} per file (PHP settings upload_max_filesize/post_max_size). A higher value only takes effect once the hoster raises these limits.

Thumbnails are created at most this wide and this high; the aspect ratio is kept. Applies to newly uploaded and replaced images; existing thumbnails stay as they are. Default: 200, allowed: {min} to {max}.

“My tasks” and the task list of the API (GET /api/_tasks) deliver at most this many tasks, newest first. Default: 500, allowed: {min} to {max}.

The database is backed up before every schema change; this many backups are kept, older ones are deleted on the next “Apply”. Default: 5 (or SCHEMA_BACKUP_KEEP from config.php), allowed: {min} to {max}.
From this database size on, System → Schema points out the disk space the backups take up together. Default: 50 (or SCHEMA_BACKUP_WARN_MB from config.php), allowed: {min} to {max}.
Every save creates a version; this many are kept per record, older ones are deleted on the next save of the record. 0 = keep all. Default: 5, allowed: {min} to {max}.

Write access is locked during a schema migration or a restore. If PHP aborts hard meanwhile, the lock stays behind; after this time it counts as orphaned and is ignored. Do not choose less than a migration takes on this server. Default: 120, allowed: {min} to {max}.
The time an API key was last used is written at most this often – not on every request. 0 = on every request (one write access per request). Default: 300, allowed: {min} to {max} (24 hours).
System → Test data creates at most this many records per entity in one run. Large amounts may exceed the execution time limit of the server. Default: 1000, allowed: {min} to {max}.
